prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map depicts a straight paved road stretching ahead in frames 1, 2, and 4, bordered by a raised curb and sloped grassy lawn on the right (~2–15 m away), trees (~10–25 m away), and a multi-story apartment building (~25–40 m away), while the camera wearer turns rightward in frames 3 and 5 to bring a companion on the right side into view at roughly 0.8–1.2 m distance. In frames 3 and 5, this companion stands within or just at the edge of the camera wearer's arm's reach on the far right, cropped at the torso and right edge of the frame, facing forward/left along the road away from the camera wearer's gaze, while the building sits ~25–35 m behind and to the left of the companion. Across the five frames, the camera wearer progresses forward along the road while alternating head turns between facing straight down the road (frames 1, 2, 4) and turning right toward the lawn and companion (frames 3, 5), with the companion's raised knee or leg appearing slightly closer in the lower-right foreground of frame 5. The depth map clearly reveals the continuous receding ground plane, the sharp vertical step of the right-hand curb, and the foreground separation of the companion against the distant lawn and trees more distinctly than RGB texture alone. However, the depth map is unreliable in its relative scale normalization across frames—causing the ground and lawn in frames 3 and 5 to appear much darker (farther) simply because the bright foreground person dominates the near-depth range—and it flattens fine distant branches and building details into uniform black.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates three distant parked cars on the far left (~40–60 m away) and the apartment building on the right (~25–40 m away, mislabeled as a 'train') in frame 1, and segments the companion on the far right foreground (~0.8–1.2 m away, within arm's reach) in frames 3 and 5. In frame 1, the three small car masks sit side-by-side to the left of the road ~50–70 m from the building on the right, whereas in frames 3 and 5 the 'person' mask occupies the lower-right corner, partially out of view beyond the right and bottom frame edges and facing left/forward without looking at the camera wearer. Across the 5 frames, the camera wearer's rightward head turns in frames 3 and 5 bring the companion's upper body (and raised leg in frame 5) into the right side of the field of view, while frames 2 and 4 contain no segmented instances as the wearer looks straight down the empty road. The segmentation map makes the tiny distant parked cars on the far left of frame 1 immediately noticeable despite their low contrast in the RGB image, and provides a sharp silhouette boundary of the companion's torso, head, and raised leg against the sunlit background. However, the map is highly unreliable for scene layout: it misclassifies the distant apartment building as a 'train' in frame 1, fails to detect the building or distant vehicles in frames 2–5, and omits static background geometry like the road, curb, lawn, and trees.
descriptions.pose: The body/hand skeleton map detects only the companion in the lower-right foreground (~0.8–1.2 m from the camera wearer, within arm's reach) during the rightward head turns in frames 3 and 5, leaving frames 1, 2, and 4 completely blank as the camera wearer looks down the open road. In frame 3, a cluster of yellow facial keypoints (eyes, nose, ears) above a short neck/shoulder segment shows the companion's head in left profile facing forward along the road and looking away from the camera wearer, with the lower torso and limbs occluded by the bottom and right edges of the frame. By frame 5, as the camera wearer turns rightward again, the skeleton expands downward to include a long torso/hip line and upper-leg segments alongside the facial keypoints, reflecting that more of the companion's right-side body and raised leg have entered the lower-right field of view. Compared to the RGB strip, the pose keypoints explicitly pin down the companion's head orientation and shoulder-to-hip alignment despite heavy cropping and harsh backlighting. However, the pose map is unreliable in completeness: it misses the companion's arms and hands entirely (no magenta keypoints appear), fails to connect the head to the shoulder in frame 3, and provides no spatial information about the surrounding road, lawn, or distant objects.
